title: The Safety Valve in Handling Complaints
coreMove: Let an upset person talk themselves empty before you say a word, then ask one question that invites more rather than less

exampleSpecs.domain: a veterinary receptionist taking a call from a man whose dog died after surgery
exampleSpecs.audience: a frontline service worker who keeps trying to explain policy over a grieving customer
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the clinic loses a twenty-year client and a public review, or keeps a relationship the vet built across two generations of dogs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the receptionist resists every urge to say 'but' or 'actually' and instead says 'tell me more about Buster' until the man is the one who eventually pauses

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school assistant principal sitting across from a parent who is convinced his daughter was unfairly suspended
exampleSpecs.audience: a school administrator who is technically correct and losing the room
exampleSpecs.stakes: a board complaint, a daughter who watches her father be dismissed, and a precedent for how the school handles future disputes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the administrator closes her laptop, pushes the discipline file to the side of the desk, and asks the father to start from the morning of the incident in his own words

exampleSpecs.domain: a union shop steward fielding a machinist's furious accusation that the new shift schedule is rigged against older workers
exampleSpecs.audience: a steward who privately agrees the machinist is wrong about the cause but right about the feeling
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wildcat walkout on Monday if the machinist leaves the meeting still hot
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the steward keeps a notepad face down and only asks one prompt every several minutes, letting silence carry more weight than counter-argument

exampleSpecs.domain: a daughter calling her recently widowed father to complain about how her brother is handling their mother's estate
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult child caught between two siblings who both feel unseen
exampleSpecs.stakes: a Thanksgiving table that may not have everyone at it again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the daughter, who came to argue, notices her father simply asking 'and what else' three times until she names the actual grief underneath the money

exampleSpecs.domain: a hotel night manager confronted at 1am by a guest whose room reeked of smoke and whose anniversary dinner reservation was lost
exampleSpecs.audience: a manager whose first instinct is to offer compensation in the first thirty seconds
exampleSpecs.stakes: a couple's tenth anniversary, the hotel's reputation on a review site read by every traveler in the city
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager catches herself reaching for the comp voucher, puts the pen down, and instead says nothing for a full ten seconds while the guest finishes her sentence and starts a new one

exampleSpecs.domain: a city council member at a town hall after a beloved oak on Maple Street was cut down by the public works department
exampleSpecs.audience: an elected official who could read out the legal justification and end the meeting in fifteen minutes
exampleSpecs.stakes: reelection, neighborhood trust, and whether the next removal will be met with a lawsuit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the meeting the council member writes down what she would have said if she had spoken first, and notices that nothing on the list would have changed a single resident's mind
